title: 1.3.17 Team Vocabulary
description: Your teammate wrote cartItems. You wrote basketItems. Say what the problem is and what you do about it. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
You have joined a team building an online shop.

1. The team calls a logged-in person a "member". Which variable name is better, currentMember or currentPerson? Say which, and why.

2. Your team calls a shopping cart a "basket". A teammate's existing code uses cartItems. Your new code uses basketItems. What is the problem this creates for anyone reading the code, and what should you do about it?

3. Suppose you genuinely prefer the word "cart" and the team has settled on "basket". What do you do, and why? Be honest about the reasoning.

rubric.title: Q1: picks currentMember and ties it to the team's word
rubric.description: Student chooses currentMember and explains that it matches the term the team already uses, keeping the vocabulary consistent. Deny if currentPerson is chosen, or if currentMember is chosen with no reason connected to team terminology.

rubric.title: Q2: names the reader's problem
rubric.description: Student identifies that a reader cannot tell whether cartItems and basketItems are two different things or the same thing under two names, or otherwise names the confusion/searchability cost of mixed vocabulary. Deny if the answer only says it is 'messy' or 'inconsistent' without saying what that costs a reader.

rubric.title: Q2: says what to do
rubric.description: Student proposes an actual action - rename to match the existing code, or agree one term with the team and change everything to it. Credit either direction as long as the outcome is ONE word used everywhere. Deny 'leave it, it's fine' or an answer with no action.

rubric.title: Q3: consistency beats personal preference
rubric.description: Student says they would use the team's word despite preferring their own, and gives a reason grounded in the codebase - one word per idea is easier to read and search, and mixed vocabulary costs everyone. Deny if the student says they would keep using their preferred word, or gives no reason beyond 'to be polite' or 'to follow rules'.
